correctness.rationale: For all convex polygons, cap areas at generic support vertices are exactly triangular at sufficiently small offsets. The exact Crofton integral, a global inball-based uniform square-root cap domination and dominated convergence yield the full formula. The strict parallelogram extremum follows from the pointwise arithmetic-geometric mean inequality and side-length AM-GM. Sharpness, regular-n and disk expansions are explicit. Standalone cap-clipping checks independently corroborate finite probabilities.

value.rationale: A natural unbiased random-cut model for all convex polygons has an exact corner-angle dust coefficient and a sharp, unattained supremum over the entire parallelogram class. The regular-polygon coefficient decays inversely with square-root side count, highlighting how the canonical invariant-line law differs structurally from boundary-start fragmentation and the smooth-disk exponent. The global sharp bound and polygon-to-disk singularity are motivated by stochastic integral geometry.
